title: Filing deadlines for suspicious activity reports
definition: The rule that a suspicious activity report is filed within a set number of calendar days from the initial detection of the activity that gave rise to the suspicion, with a shorter period where no earlier report has been filed for the subject, and an extension available only where the delay is explained by circumstances outside the institution's control. A continuing-activity report is due on its own cycle while the activity continues. The periods themselves are stated in the source and change; this record summarises the structure.
evidence_to_cite: the initial detection date, and how it was established
the filing date of the report, and any justification for a delay
the basis for the continued-activity cycle used, where one applies

sources.citation: Suspicious activity reporting filing deadlines, including the continuing-activity rule (31 CFR 1020.320), summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: The deadline runs from detection, not from the transaction. A record of the detection date is the single most important thing to keep.
